question: What station-resolved fish research does Jumawan, Salunga and Catap (2010) report for Marikina River, and can its Pterygoplichthys label be resolved or counted independently from the same-title 2009 NAST abstract and related Marikina studies?

source.title: Lipid Peroxidation and Patterns of Cadmium and Lead Accumulation in the Vital Organs of the Suckermouth Armored Catfish Pterygoplichthys Gill, 1858 from Marikina River, Philippines
source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., Salunga, T. P., & Catap, E. S. (2010). Lipid Peroxidation and Patterns of Cadmium and Lead Accumulation in the Vital Organs of the Suckermouth Armored Catfish Pterygoplichthys Gill, 1858 from Marikina River, Philippines. Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation, 5(4), 375-390, October-December 2010.
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the full-text mirror's bibliographic information, abstract, materials and methods, station descriptions, and taxon labels. The mirror identifies the original journal and publisher site; the publisher site could not be independently retrieved during this review. No article PDF, figure, table, or raw measurements were retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The full-text mirror states that the article is open access under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC BY 3.0). This license statement was not verified against an accessible publisher-hosted copy. Only minimal citation and methodological facts are summarized; the article, map, tables, images, and measurements are not redistributed. Publication approval is false.

studyDesign.studyPurpose: Historical tissue-metal accumulation and lipid-peroxidation research on locally collected suckermouth armored catfish, with separate commercially supplied control fish.

sample.allocation: 17 fish per each of four sampling stations
sample.controlTreatment: The article distinguishes 20 store-supplied, farm-raised fish used as controls from the 68 fish collected locally at the four river stations. The controls are not Marikina River captures.
sample.gearAsReported: Cast net, 3.5 m, mesh size 3.8 cm

samplingLocalitiesAsReported.locality: Along the banks of Marikina River Park
Downstream along Marikina River Banks Mall, Barangay Barangka

dateAndSpatialLimits.fieldCollectionDate: Not stated in the reviewed article text.
dateAndSpatialLimits.publicationDates: The article reports received, revised, and accepted dates in 2010. These editorial dates do not establish when fish were collected.
dateAndSpatialLimits.coordinates: No verifiable station coordinates or station-to-specimen identifiers were found in the reviewed text. The published figure was not digitized or georeferenced.
dateAndSpatialLimits.vouchers: No voucher catalogue numbers or sequence accessions were identified for the 68 fish in the reviewed article. This is not evidence that vouchers do not exist elsewhere.

studyDesign.localityInterpretation: The article names four station contexts along one river system and allocates 17 sampled fish to each station, but it provides no coordinate or individually identifiable specimen crosswalk. Retain the source's station labels as research context only; do not create map points, exact capture coordinates, city assignments, or public occurrence rows from the article figure.
studyDesign.samplingLimit: This was targeted host-fish research for a tissue and stress study, not a standardized fish-community inventory, population estimate, fishery assessment, or current-presence survey.

identityAndStudyLineage.sourceLabelDecision: Preserve the 2010 article's Pterygoplichthys spp. label at genus level. Do not promote the source label to P. pardalis or P. disjunctivus.

sameTitle2009Abstract.relationship: The NAST Transactions abstract has the same study title, shares Jumawan and Catap, lists Salunga with a different middle initial (L. rather than P.), and gives a four-site Marikina River context. Treat it as a likely related earlier presentation, but preserve the author-initial and sample-lineage uncertainties. Its wording calls the fish Pterygoplichthys pardalis; the 2010 article's methods and figure captions use Pterygoplichthys spp. The abstract does not identify individual specimens or establish cohort overlap.
sameTitle2009Abstract.chronologyCaveat: The NAST volume describes papers presented at the 31st Annual Scientific Meeting on 8-9 July 2009, while the journal article was received in September 2010. Neither the presentation date nor the article's editorial dates are fish-collection dates. The chronology and unavailable field dates prevent a reliable sample-cohort crosswalk.
sameTitle2009Abstract.decision: Do not treat the abstract as independent confirmation of P. pardalis or count it as a second survey. Preserve the species-label discrepancy, author-initial discrepancy, and unresolved cohort identity.

relatedMarikinaStudies.relationship: The 2011 COI study reports 36 Pterygoplichthys samples from five Marikina River-system stations and finds that DNA barcodes do not consistently complement morphology-based P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus identification. It does not identify this 2010 article's 68 fish as the same specimens.

The 2016 article reports a separate 2010-2011 host-fish study under the label P. disjunctivus. Its collection period overlaps the 2010 journal publication year, but the 2010 article gives no field dates and no sample crosswalk; cohort overlap and independent-sample status are unresolved.

identityAndStudyLineage.independenceDecision: Treat the 2010 article and same-title 2009 conference abstract as a likely related research lineage, not two independent surveys; the Salunga middle initial also differs between the records. Do not merge its 68-fish sample with the 2011 barcode or 2010-2011 life-history samples without specimen-level documentation.

reuseAndSafety.licenseDecision: The accessible full-text mirror prints a CC BY 3.0 notice. The original publisher-hosted page was not independently verified in this review; retain that provenance caveat and do not redistribute the article or its tables, map, or measurements.
reuseAndSafety.safetyDecision: The paper's historical tissue and stress research is not a current river-water, fish-consumption, or site-safety assessment. No food-safety, water-safety, legal, or fishing recommendation can be derived for Bangwit.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain as historical research-only evidence that 68 source-labeled Pterygoplichthys spp. were sampled across four named Marikina River stations, 17 per station, using cast nets. Preserve the 2009 abstract's conflicting P. pardalis label and unresolved cohort lineage. Do not add a canonical species assertion, occurrence row, coordinate, geometry, image, safety claim, or public app projection.

nonClaims: The NAST conference date and the 2010 article's editorial dates are not field collection dates.

The same-title 2009 NAST abstract's P. pardalis label and Salunga middle initial differ from the 2010 article record; this does not override the journal article's genus-level methods label or independently identify the 68 fish.
The 68 fish are not a river population estimate, standardized community survey, fishery landing, catch-per-unit-effort, or complete Marikina River checklist.
The four locality names and station sample counts do not justify coordinate points, an administrative-boundary assignment, or a geometry derived from the article figure.
No specimen-level linkage was established with the 2011 DNA-barcode study or the 2010-2011 life-history study.
The study does not establish current fish presence, abundance, invasive status, catchability, fishing access, legal harvest, fish-consumption safety, water safety, or diet guidance.
nextActions: Keep the article and same-title NAST abstract in the Marikina research-only lineage; do not create public species, occurrence, image, or safety content from them.
Only revisit species-level identification or study independence if source-linked voucher identifiers, specimen lists, or field-collection dates become available.
Continue NCR freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland source discovery; NCR, CALABARZON, and Luzon remain incomplete.
